answer: A datacenter or proxy pool as a result cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch however much capital it holds, because each member consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. The jetty cap is enforced at intake and voyage exposes the per-origin counts. At most 1 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a terrace tag. That is 30 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
